fields.title: From metric change to root cause
fields.keyTakeaway: You don't cycle through hypotheses — you lay them out in a tree and cut them down with breakdowns. Each branch is either ruled out by data you already have, or stays. Usually, you are left with two or three, not ten.
fields.checkQuestion: A metric dropped by 8%. Where do you start if the team has six hypotheses?
fields.blocks/0/text: The node's key question: **why did these changes happen, and where is the growth point?** The question is not "what happened", but "which of this is the root cause".
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer the question.** A meeting is called where everyone pitches their own hypothesis. They test the one proposed by the most persuasive person, and if it's not confirmed, they start over.
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **1. Break the metric down into components.** Orders = users × active share × frequency.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **2. Find which component changed.** Usually just one.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **3. Slice it by dimensions you already have** — segment, platform, source, version, geography.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **4. Stop where you can act on the cause.** "People stopped wanting it as much" is not a cause.
fields.blocks/3/text: The main time-saver is step 3: a slice rules out entire branches in minutes. If the drop is isolated to a single platform, all hypotheses about price, seasonality, and marketing fall away immediately.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Metric: number of closed schedules per week. Broken down: accounts × share of those closing × frequency. The second one changed — the share.

Slices: by platform — drop only on Android; by app version — only on the version released three weeks ago; by account size — same across all.

The team's six hypotheses — seasonality, prices, competitor, churn, marketing, quality — fell away on the very first breakdown. The root cause was found in an hour: in the new Android version, the publish button slipped under the keyboard on screens of a certain height.
fields.blocks/5/text: A tree works when a metric breaks down into parts and you have dimensions. If there are few dimensions or events are rare, several branches will remain — then it's more honest to say "narrowed down to two" than to pick one and call it the root cause.
